LOOK: Clients transact at the Land Transportation Office (LTO) Regional Office 11 “LTO on Wheels” bus in Buhangin, Davao City, on Tuesday, Jan. 6.

The mobile unit is deployed as a temporary service site after the LTO satellite office inside Gaisano Grand Citygate Mall remains closed due to a fire on Jan. 2.

The LTO on Wheels caters to applications for Student Permits, driver’s license renewals, motor vehicle renewals, and the issuance of motorcycle plates. The bus will remain beside the mall until further notice, according to LTO Davao Region.

📷: Keith Bacongco | MB

data.text:
If we look back just 10 years ago, Filipino Christmas traditions were very manual, and almost everything was a high-effort labor of love. Christmas in the Philippines has always been a season of joy, family gatherings, and the cherished tradition of gift-giving. For decades, malls and bazaars were the beating heart of holiday shopping, with Filipinos flocking to crowded stores to find the perfect presents. Most of us endured intense gridlock, last-minute gift panic-buying, and the frantic morning rush for Noche Buena ingredients.
